facts.about: Interglobe Aviation Ltd (Indigo) is India’s largest passenger airline operating as a low-cost carrier. Serving 86 destinations including 24 international destinations, it provides passengers with a simple, unbundled product, fulfilling its singular brand promise of providing “low fares, on-time flights, and a courteous and hassle-free service” to its customers. IndiGo commenced operations in August 2006 with a single aircraft and has grown its fleet to 262 aircrafts.

flags.text: Cash-rich profits: 5-yr operating cash = 1274% of PAT

business.summary: InterGlobe Aviation Limited operates passenger airline services, primarily through its brand IndiGo, generating revenue from passenger transportation ticket sales, cancellation fees, and related ancillary services.

narrative.scoreline: Management delivers on unit revenue expansion promises but faces severe profitability headwinds and missed Q4 FY26 volume targets.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: InterGlobe reported total income of ₹256 billion, up ~19% YoY in Q1 FY27.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Jun 2026 quarterly revenue came in at ₹24,584 cr, growing 19.9% YoY.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Management reported a net loss of ₹19 billion in Q2 FY27 due to fuel costs and soft demand.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Sep 2026 quarter reported a net loss of ₹1,879 cr with operating margins declining to 8%.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Reported net loss of ₹2.4 billion in Q1 FY27.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Jun 2026 quarter posted a PAT loss of ₹238 cr.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Rupee depreciation generated net forex losses of ₹10.4 billion in Q3 FY26.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Full-year FY26 net profit swung to a loss of ₹2,394 cr from ₹7,258 cr in FY25.

bull: Sep 2026 top-line revenue expanded 25.9% YoY to ₹23,364 cr driven by strong unit yields.
FY26 cash generation remained robust with operating cash flow of ₹23,470 cr and FCF of ₹21,767 cr.
5-year aggregate operating cash flow represents 1274% of cumulative net profit.
bear: Full-year FY26 profitability crashed to a net loss of ₹2,394 cr versus ₹7,258 cr profit in FY25.
Balance sheet leverage remains extreme with debt-to-equity at 17.47x on ₹87,303 cr total borrowings.
Losses persisted into FY27 with Sep 2026 net loss reaching ₹1,879 cr.
watch: Return to net profitability in Q3 FY27 following two consecutive quarterly losses.
Achievement of >25% YoY PRASK expansion guidance in Dec 2026 quarter.

claims.claim: Reported a net loss of 19 billion rupees due to exceptionally high fuel costs and seasonally soft demand.
claims.quote: However, due to the elevated cost environment, we reported a net loss of 19 billion rupees.

claims.claim: Ended the quarter with total cash of 527 billion rupees, including 399 billion rupees of free cash.
claims.quote: Our liquidity remains strong, with free cash of around 399 billion rupees.

claims.claim: Inducted 22 aircraft and redelivered 10 aircraft plus 2 damp-leased aircraft, ending with 442 aircraft.
claims.quote: During the quarter, we inducted a total of 22 aircraft from our original orderbook... resulting in a total closing fleet of 442 aircraft at the quarter-end.

claims.claim: Reported total income of 256 billion rupees, up about 19% YoY, with yield growth of 21.3%.
claims.quote: we reported a total income of 256 billion rupees, a growth of around 19% year over year, with a yield growth of 21.3% and a load factor reduction of 1.3%.

claims.claim: EBITDAR came in at 38.3 billion rupees at 15.6% margin; reported a net loss of 2.4 billion rupees.
claims.quote: In terms of profitability, EBITDAR came in at 38.3 billion rupees at a margin of 15.6% compared to an EBITDAR of 57.4 billion rupees and a margin of 28% for the same period last year. For the quarter we reported a net loss of 2.4 billion rupees

claims.claim: June quarter capacity growth came in at 3% YoY, broadly in line with guidance.
claims.quote: June quarter’s capacity growth came in at 3% on a year-over-year basis, broadly in line with our guidance.

claims.claim: Fuel CASK increased by around 80% year-on-year due to geopolitical volatility and crack spreads.
claims.quote: Despite this measure, our fuel CASK increased by around 80% year-on-year.

claims.claim: Inducted 13 aircraft, redelivered 9 from original orderbook and 13 damp-leased aircraft, closing fleet at 432.
claims.quote: We inducted a total of 13 aircraft from our original orderbook... We redelivered 9 aircraft from our original orderbook and 13 damp-leased aircraft during the quarter resulting in a total closing fleet of 432 aircraft at the quarter end.

claims.claim: Operational disruptions in early December led to cancellations of over 2,500 flights and hundreds of delays between December 3rd and 5th.
claims.quote: Now, I want to address the operational disruptions that began in the first week of December and that led to cancellations of more than 2,500 flights and delays of hundreds of flights during the period of 3rd to 5th December.

claims.claim: IndiGo received 57 aircraft deliveries from the original orderbook in calendar year 2025 and was the largest Airbus recipient globally.
claims.quote: In terms of fleet addition, in the calendar year 2025 we received deliveries of 57 aircraft from our original orderbook – 55 A320 family aircraft and 2 ATR aircraft. An important milestone is our position as the largest recipient of Airbus aircraft globally for the second consecutive year

claims.claim: Depreciation of the rupee by about 5% over 12 months led to a net forex loss of 10.4 billion rupees.
claims.quote: As you are aware the rupee has depreciated significantly in the last 12 months by around 5%. Rupee depreciated by more than 1% at the third quarter end as compared to the second quarter end leading to a forex loss net of hedging of 10.4 billion rupees
